HEEWON STYLE — a KOREAN WEBTOON movie still PAINTED like a premium digital painting, the look of a dramatic manhwa cover. A 2:1 movie frame composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop (nothing important at the top or bottom edge). The shot the scene names (wide establishing, two-shot, close-up, over-the-shoulder) from a dramatic camera angle (low three-quarter, worm's-eye, high overhead or dutch), never a flat straight-on catalogue pose. Named characters' FACES are drawn exactly like the attached character sheet: the same clean confident ink linework and manhwa face design (eye shape, brows, nose, jaw, hairline and hair), recognisably those characters, in the clothes the scene gives them. EVERYTHING ELSE IS PAINTED: visible textured brushwork — loose digital-paint strokes and dry-brush, charcoal-like hatching that follow every fold of the silk and every plate of armour, the shadows built from layered strokes, the brightest ridges laid in with single confident strokes, a faint paper-and-canvas grain; at the edges of the garments the linework breaks into loose sketchy strokes. NOT flat cel-shading, NOT smooth airbrushed gradients, NOT a clean vector look, NOT photoreal, NOT 3D. Interior of an open timber pavilion built over a great flat boulder, the Rock of Politics, in Sabi. Worm's-eye from the rock surface. Tiers of low benches crowded with princes in Baekje court robes and feather caps, all heads turned toward a tall painted folding screen at the side. Prince Yung, cold and proud in pale gold, in the foreground half-turned, smirking. Prince Hyo, earnest, standing mid-word. Behind the screen's edge, Queen Eungo's face in profile, composed, eyes lowered. Daylight shaft through the eaves cutting the screen in half; dusty rose #c9a0a8 catching her silk at the gap. CHARACTER SHEET, left to right: LEFT face = yung, SECOND face = hyo, THIRD face = ungo. Copy each face exactly; give each person the dress the scene names. PRINCE YUNG — Look: Prince of Baekje in his late forties: broad calm face, high black topknot, thin moustache and small chin beard, heavy-lidded eyes that give nothing away. Dress: Baekje prince's red robe with black outer sleeves and gold cloud-scroll collar and shoulders, red cord sash with long tassels. Colour #d4b45a. PRINCE HYO Colour #c9a86a. QUEEN EUNGO — Crown: Baekje king: a tall rounded black silk cap (오라관) with a plain black band at the brow, and a pair of tall openwork gold flame-and-leaf ornaments (금제관식) pinned to either side of the cap, rising above it like twin flames — thin gold blades fanning upward with leaf buds and curls. Colour #c9a0a8. BACKGROUND AND LIGHT (painterly tenebrism): the background IS the place and the moment of the scene — open sky if they are in the sky, the hall if they are in a hall, the gate, the river, the snow — painted loosely in atmospheric brushwork (drifting smoke, cloud, haze, mist, falling snow, embers) in the scene's own colours, soft and out of focus, with a faint bokeh of small lights; it has colour, weather and depth — never a flat black void, never a detailed set; crowds and armies only as massed painted shapes dissolving into haze. ONE hard directional key light that belongs to the place (a brazier, a lamp, the sun through cloud, a torch, moonlight) rakes across the faces and clothes from the side or from below, modelling them in high contrast with deep painted shadows and a thin edge of the same light along the silhouette. Each character's colour lives in that light and in the atmosphere around them — never a glow aura or halo. Faces and bodies act the beat: real expressions, real weight, mid-motion. Faces from the sheet; new poses, never the sheet's stance. Each named person appears once, never cloned. Everyone wears period clothing of their own court (Korean, Tang, Yamato, Mohe furs), never European dress. No text, no speech bubbles, no panel borders, no watermark.
